title: Travel Cost Calibration for Multi-Agent Target Assignment and Pathfinding
title_zh: 面向多智能体目标分配与寻路的旅行成本校准

paragraphs.en: 通过从次优MAPF反馈校准旅行成本，迭代改进多智能体目标分配质量。 Target assignment and pathfinding (TAPF) is an appealing extension of classical multi-agent pathfinding (MAPF): each agent has a set of targets, and the planner must both assign a target to each agent and plan collision-free paths for them. A trivial approach is to compute an assignment that minimizes the total single-agent shortest-path distance over agent--target pairs, and then solve the resulting MAPF instance. However, this approach falls short because the shortest-path distance remains a proxy that ignores interference among agents. Assigning targets based on the costs agents actually pay, which depend on how every other agent is assigned and routed, would yield a better final outcome. To this end, we propose an iterative TAPF method that improves target assignments by calibrating travel cost estimates from fast, suboptimal MAPF feedback. Experiments show that our method produces solutions close to optimal on small instances and outperforms existing planners in solution quality on larger ones.
paragraphs.zh: 通过从次优MAPF反馈校准旅行成本，迭代改进多智能体目标分配质量。目标分配与路径规划（TAPF）是经典多智能体路径规划（MAPF）的一个颇具吸引力的扩展：每个智能体拥有一组目标，规划器必须为每个智能体分配一个目标，并为它们规划无碰撞路径。 一种简单直接的做法是先计算一个使所有智能体—目标对的单智能体最短路径距离总和最小的分配方案，然后再求解由此得到的MAPF实例。 然而，这种做法存在不足，因为最短路径距离只是一个代理指标，忽略了智能体之间的相互干扰。 基于智能体实际付出的成本来分配目标会带来更好的最终结果，而这些成本取决于其他所有智能体如何被分配和规划路径。 为此，我们提出一种迭代式TAPF方法，通过从快速、次优的MAPF反馈中校准旅行成本估计来改进目标分配。 实验表明，我们的方法在小规模实例上能产生接近最优的解，在更大规模实例上解的质量优于现有规划器。
